claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Surface aluminizing, such as pack cementation, can deposit an Al-rich coating on as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminizing equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will produce a thin, continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale during exposure to air at 800 °C.
Al introduced by aluminizing will preferentially oxidize to Al2O3.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a diffusion barrier and slow oxygen ingress.
Slower oxygen ingress will mitigate oxidation pesting of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
A surface aluminizing treatment will not alter the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical properties.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, aluminized material will have a thinner and more stable oxide layer than untreated material.
Aluminized material will retain room-temperature ductility similar to untreated material.
Aluminized material will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to untreated material.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr rapidly oxidizes or pests during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
Oxidation of untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr degrades its mechanical performance.
The proposed protection is expected to remain effective around 800 °C for exposures up to 5 hours.
Excessive coating thickness, loss of adherence, or mechanical damage may limit protection.
Higher strain rates or repeated thermal cycling may compromise coating performance.
The coating process may introduce microstructural defects that impair mechanical performance.
